reviews.text: I feel like I was living at this place for the better part of a week when a recent minor change to my cat's diet resulted in multiple visits, a two-night stay for gastroenteritis, and then a subsequent cystitis flare due to the stressful situation all before I was due to be out of town for a week!  It was an incredibly stressful situation for me as well and I can't say enough about how helpful, kind, and patient the staff here was with me and my cat (esp. Dr. Russell)!  The communication was top-notch.  They answered all my questions, talked me through all of the treatment, and even prescribed additional meds as needed after my cat was back home.  While I hope it's a very long time before I have to be back at this place, I highly recommend them if you need emergency pet care!  Everyone here rocks!

Whoever was on staff including security from the hours of 9 pm to 12:45 am from 10/15 to early hours of 10/16….you guys rock. I lost my mind tonight thinking I was potentially going to lose my baby. Not only were every single one of you beyond professional and kind, you all took the time to actually care about not only my girl (Squishyy) but ME as a person. I cannot thank the triage, front desk, security, the doctor, just ALL OF YOU. Thank you for letting me anxiety rant and even one of your staff who I was just able to relate to over school and similar friends in overlapping fields (girl you know who you are and I seriously appreciate you, same to the person who i talked to on the phone and initially checked us in). I was brought water, snacks, and just given the utmost reassurance about everything happening. I literally was laying on the floor half asleep with her (she hid under the couch) as I had no idea what was going on for a bit (normal for an ER vet), and you all just offered a kind hand, listening ear, and overall the most sincere care. Not to mention no price gouging, no “well she might need this so we’ll do it anyway”. Clear treatment plan. If it isn’t working? Come back and we’ll go on to more imaging and bloodwork, etc. I can’t express how grateful I am for every single one of you and how much I commend you all for the job you do everyday because it can’t be easy. Thank you for your love and care for not only my sweet Squishyy, but me as well.

THIS is the place to go if your pet is having an emergency. I just spent two nights here with my pup while he was having a severe health issue, and I will likely rave about this team for the rest of time.

We were greeted and triaged promptly, treated swiftly and with kindness, my dog's care was managed thoughtfully, and the team was consistent on checking in on my wellbeing, too.

Drs. Russell and Parker were wonderful team leads, and the nurses and techs (Georgia, Katie, Amanda and Jackie) were *so* on top of things. By the time we left, my dog was licking the vet's face. No better emergency vet review than that!

I also noticed how grounded and caring the team was while handling difficult emergency situations, aside from my own pet's condition.This team kept their heads on and their hearts open. Not easy to do. A+++ 100000, everybody! Thanks, VEG team! We love you. - Julia and Dylan

Hi Soa! We truly appreciate your 5-star rating! It means a lot to us to hear that you had a positive experience. Thank you for taking the time to share your thoughts. - Elliot Won, Sr. Hospital Manager

I am beyond happy with our experience at VEG this evening. TLDR: Virtually no wait time; Vet tech checked my baby right away while we waited for a doctor; Staff was super gentle, attentive, and caring; Dr. Libby Martin was incredibly patient with questions and easy to understand; Overall cost was way less than I expected; Overall visit was way shorter than I expected (about an hour total).

I went into this ER expecting it to be chaotic and to be there all night. Was also worried about being pressured into a bunch of tests and procedures that may or may not have been necessary. Turns out I didn't need to worry about any of that. The overall vibe felt pretty laid back, yet very professional and efficient. Was expecting a stressful, anxiety inducing visit (especially since I was already worried about my furbaby), but was pleasantly surprised.

10/10 would recommend to anyone seeking emergency vet services. Appreciate everything that these folx do!!

Hi Tanya! Thank you for your wonderful 5-star rating! We're truly grateful to hear that your experience with us was positive, as it reflects the strong sense of unity we strive to create together. - Elliot Won, Sr. Hospital Manager

This is why I did not call, I should not come for a second visit and here yall complaining about my google review. do your job properly and fairly then a negative review wouldn’t happen. The experience I had went from 5 stars to 3 stars when one of the staff members thought FALSE IMPRISONMENT would make the perfect lasting impression. Now I have to find another exotics vet, possibly farther away, to avoid feeling like a statistic! Stop judging people and JUST do your job.
Hi Josh! Thank you for your 5-star rating! We're thrilled to hear that you had a positive experience with us. - Elliot Won, Sr. Hospital Manager

Worst place to bring your animal , sat for 4 hours with a hole in my dogs neck and nothing was told they can’t give me a estimate time when my dog would be seen , non emergency animals seen before my dog , stuff is very unprofessional and rude , please don’t bring your animal here if you have an emergency!!!

Coming here was stressful which everyone knows coming here is a life or death situation.  The staff at this facility is very kind and helps with the process of helping each and every fur babie and us partners. The staff took my cat right away. I like to say each and every person worked with heart and soul.  They did what ever they needed to help the fur babies.

I like to call out Dr. Giana she is an amazing doctor. She went above and beyond to help my babg.Nurse Jacqulyn great nurse. Vincent who help walk me through the financial aspect and explained everything thoroughly. And the guard even was so nice and make it a little easier in this time of need.

I like to thank the who staff for all your help with helping my fur

We were greeted then kind of left in the desk area .
Another customer came in ,she was taken before us .
A  different young lady finally came out with a computer, asked a few questions. She was brisk and unfriendly .Would not let me talk ,seemed to shut me down .
Our dog was in bad shape,we were in bad shape .I'm 69 years old BTW and didnt need the reception or attitude.
Really doesn't matter how old I am I suppose but very put of by the second young lady who we interacted with .

The guard was lovey. Personable and nice .

We came in during the evening hours .

Also ,we didn't receive a card after the fact as I see you do .

I was totally blown away by the level of care they provided us. From the moment we walked in scared for my girl Luna to the moment we left knowing we have many healthy years ahead. Do not go anywhere else if you truly love your animal!

Honestly, I had a very different review written that was posted for a few days. I had a less than ideal experience at this location due to the doctor that was on the case. As pet owners having to visit an emergency vet, obviously we are terrified and upset and expecting the Worst. The Bedside mannerism from the doctor was extremely undesirable, but everything else was great from reception to the nurse (Nicole) that took care of my baby.  After my very unhappy review, I was reached out to to talk about my experience and rectify the situation. I do feel as though it was handled well, and I have even had to reach out since as I will be out of pain management before my cats scheduled amputation to which I was responded to promptly and told that they would be happy to help me out, regardless of what happened. We all hope to never need an emergency vet but I can truthfully say that VEG in Northern Liberties is a great place full of love. We all have bad days, and I’m sorry to the doctor on the case that we added to it.

I want to say thank you to the team that took me in and answered my questions, shown great compassion for the hardest choice I ever had to do and that was saying good bye to my baby boy Bentley. Their end of life program was as smooth as it could be and they helped me with my options with going forward in letting him go. They work with a great cremation company called paws to heaven and Keith was an amazing and kind person in understanding my grief as well.

I am ever so grateful to have been accompanied by a wonderful team with phenomenal service at the ER at Veg. Everyone who assisted in the care for my dog during her Life’s transition was just overall superbly supportive and God-given angels with warm, comforting support and expertise. They provided necessary information, they directed us to the best support services they had available and supported us with a warm and comforting environment during our emergency stay. I cried the entire time so I don’t remember everyone’s names expect Bee. Thanks a Million Veg ER team.

Dr Crutchlow + staff provided phenomenal care, checked in frequently with updates and next steps, explained everything thoroughly, offered snack/water, and had amazing bedside manner. Very grateful for the care they provided.

My dog moo was so sick and i thought near death. The staff was extremely friendly and caring. They helped me with everything from the moment i walked through the front door until the very end when a staff member helped me carry moo to my car.  The doctors were very gentle and loving with her. She is normally very rambunctious and aggressive. They showed no fear and tackled the job at hand. I can write an entire book about the care moo  recieved here. I wanna give a huge shout out to Dr. Bush, Dr. G, Floyd and especially Ashlynn. You are truely amazing people. I will 1000% recommend Northern liberty veg for anyone in need. Thank you all so much♥️

What a great experience in the face of hardship. My dog is my baby and she received the best treatment all 3 times we had to be there. Everyone at VEG truly made us feel so safe and cared for, we couldn’t have asked for better treatment. Thank you all so much! Please if you need emergent care for you fur baby come see the staff at VEG!

I brought my cat in last night because he was having a urinary blockage. From the minute I arrived, I felt the genuine concern and care from the staff there. They allowed me to stay with Cheddar the whole time petting him while they took care of him. They explained everything as clearly as possible and were so kind. After he was treated, they gave me a week’s supply of the new food he has to eat. I am eternally grateful for them for saving my sweet angel. The entire staff at Northern Liberties is exceptional.

The VEG team were very attentive and informative. My bunny was rushed for early signs of GI stasis and was seen immediately. I'm glad that VEG is here for all fur babies in need of emergency, thank you!

Dr Hoffman, lead veterinary tech/specialist and the entire team at VEG saved my dog’s life from an inadvertent exposure to a lethal street drug on the floor of a restaurant (Jaxx’s on Moyamensing Ave in Pennsport)! I couldn’t be more thankful for the expeditious, decisive, comprehensive and compassionate care my sweet Berkeley received!!

Went to VEG three times in one week. Not only was there ample parking and security but the staff was incredible. I think I met like 15 people over Rosie's visits/stay and every single one of them was the most kind and empathetic person, towards the dog and myself. The facility is clean and they work quickly while also prioritizing emergencies. Rosie ended up having to stay overnight Friday and they even offered me a couch to sleep on if I wanted to stay with her. She's still feelin it but without VEG, she might have had severe complications from dehydration, malnutrition, and her digestive issues and I might have had an anxiety attack.

I wish there was 6 stars, the facility was very good, clean, and fully set up for any issue with all the newest equipment but the staff was absolutely incredible. I watched them console more than one pet owner who got bad news and they were more kind than human doctors I have encountered.

I cannot express enough gratitude to the incredible team at VEG Northern Liberties. When Baskota was attacked and injured by a neighbor’s dog, it was one of the scariest moments of my life. We came in for two separate visits—first for urgent emergency intervention and later for follow-up care—and the care across both was nothing short of phenomenal.

From the second we walked through the doors during the initial crisis, the staff stepped in with swift expertise, calm, and genuine empathy. Being able to stay right by Baskota’s side the entire time gave both of us immense peace of mind during a terrifying ordeal. Returning for our second visit, every doctor and nurse showed that same consistent gentleness, attentiveness, and deep knowledge, thoroughly checking his healing and never making us feel rushed.

Their transparency, professionalism, and heartfelt compassion turned a traumatic situation into a smooth road to recovery. Baskota is healing wonderfully thanks to their dedication. If you ever find yourself facing a pet emergency, there is truly no place I would trust more than VEG Northern Liberties.
Waited almost 3 hours, they don't care if your dog is sick, bad service
Best in philly

Hi Jennifer! Thank you for your fantastic 5-star rating! We’re thrilled to hear that you had a great experience with us, and we’re committed to continually innovating to make it even better. - Elliot Won, Sr. Hospital Manager
Most expensive place did nothing until I paid  1,500 then want a 1,000 a night if he stayed plus 7,000 paid up front for surgery
Received prompt service and treatment from the moment we arrived.  Not just me and my pet, but everyone who came through the door that day with a sick pet.  Awesome care and service!
Chris was the best nurse to our guy, Bowie.

Our experience the other night was nothing short of exceptional.  We arrived around 2am Saturday morning with a sudden medical emergency Rupert.  The team welcomed us in with grace and hospitality.  Triage was immediate, results were swift, and the dedicated team took handled our circumstance with the utmost professionalism and  understanding.  These situations are always stressful and emotional, and I cannot thank the team enough for how well the they treated not only our pet - but us individually as well.

I hope there is never an emergency where one of our little ones need treatment, but if there ever is we wouldn’t trust any other team.  I cannot thank you all enough.

Zero stars if I could!!  had a terrible experience here.  I was met with friendly faces when I brought my sick dog in, but I waited over an hour and a half for a doctor to even look at my dog. I watched as the one vet walked around to check on the patients and the other vet just sat there—they were unprofessional and did not have a serious demeanor like ER doctors should.  Patients came in after me, got seen first and left before me.  They ran a ton of tests on my dog and had no urgency in talking to me or about treatment.  The bill ran up to $2500 and they gave him fluid and anti nausea meds.  The front desk was wonderful but the actual medical staff was terrible.  My dog has terrible anxiety so being there for 5 hours was awful for him.  It would have been caring and empathetic if someone came over to check on us, but they barely did.  Even when I was discharged, the vet tech spoke to me—the vet didn’t say 2 words.  Animals are our family and need to be treated better!

I have been to veg a handful of times. A few times for my cats constipation issues, once when my dog had passed at home and they handled after care and then recently at their new location to euthanize my sick cat. Each time the staff had been nothing but empathetic and kind. Most recently Dr Brodsky who helped us, was so compassionate, took her time as did the rest of the staff, and made a hard experience somewhat easier with how great she was. I can’t say enough nice things about the team at Veg and how empathetic and compassionate they always are and the top tier care you get whether it’s a small emergency or end of life care.
I called asked a question about a kitten & received a free consultation great advise things worked out just fine just!!! 😊 thank you …

The staff here are exceptionally kind and supportive. We were given an incredible amount of graciousness and support that can only be given by true lovers of animals and their humans. We were in disbelief and rage that this was her time but we were allowed to hold space. This matters so much. My girl Beauty has crossed the rainbow bridge but in her time on earth she has literally summited mountains, helped our family foster eight different dogs, helped me train dogs with her neutrality, gone on a road trip across the US stopping in every state, peed on the worlds largest rose bush, and moved cross-country. In two years she has done more than many dogs and people do in their lifetime. VEG was the best place we could have come to. Thank you.
The staff here are phenomenal. I can’t thank them and Dr Libby Martin enough for their kind, prompt and comprehensive care. Would absolutely recommend!

I had to bring by cat in for complications related to his diabetes around midnight on a Saturday night. I spoke with two people on the phone who were kind and helpful. As soon as I arrived at the ER my cat was taken care of and treatment started. I was nervous but I really appreciated how all the nurses and doctors stayed calm, which made me feel less worried, while also acting with a sense of urgency to take care of my pet. The treatment plan for my cat was clearly outlined to me, and I also felt supported when taking my cat back home. I hope I never need to bring a pet to the ER, but overall the experience went as well as I could have hoped!
Thank you to the incredible team at VEG Etobicoke for taking care of my sweet Duke on a busy Friday afternoon!
Really appreciated the care and welcoming attitude of the staff. Everyone was helpful and treated my dog with genuine care.

I came in at 2am on Friday 14 August with my three cats who I suspected had ingested Ibuprofen. One of them was already showing neurological symptoms. I was given the most professional, kind, and caring support throughout the next few days as one of my three cats had to be hospitalized for 48 hours.

Every single person on staff was so considerate and empathetic that I felt very comfortable leaving my sweet little sick cat with them. They allowed me to bring my two other cats in to spend time with my sick cat so he would feel better, and that really comforted them all. I cannot thank the staff enough for taking such great care of my little Monkey! I am so grateful he made a full recovery!

Dr. Gigantino and Dr. Chatterjee were so amazingly detailed with the information they gave me and they helped me understand what was happening, what might happen, and what we needed to do. I felt like I was kept informed of all options. Chris was absolutely wonderful and so kind with how supportive and attentive he was in making sure we were comfortable staying there for many hours over several days. I appreciate every single person who helped us and Monkey is back at home being a good little boy now!

I cannot even begin to say how caring and compassionate these people are. Unlike most money hungry vet offices, these people were right to the rescue when my husband and I brought our dog in with a pyometra case. Money wasn't even a topic until she was examined and ultrasounded. Dr. I believe her name maybe maci I cannot think , and also emalee , she was so comforting to talk to and really cares. We left with antibiotics, fluids given and referrals for emergency surgery. While our dog is not fully out of the woods yet, if it wasn't for them our kid would not be alive right now. Was referred to have emergency spaying done and she's recovering now. Thank you from the bottom of our hearts.

They also have a charity fund that helps families or individuals who may be low income or who cannot afford pet care, please consider donating to a wonderful cause .

Dr. Russell, Nurse Shannon, and the entire team at VEG Northern Liberties were absolutely amazing. From the moment Stella and I walked through the door, we were warmly greeted and immediately assisted. We were taken directly into the treatment area, where I was able to stay right beside my fur baby. They checked her vital signs, made sure I knew where the restroom was, and even showed me the complimentary snacks and beverages.

We didn’t have to wait long before Dr. Russell came over, listened carefully as I explained why we were there, and thoroughly evaluated Stella. He quickly identified what was causing her pain and explained everything clearly. Stella received pain medication by injection, and we were sent home with additional medication to keep her comfortable.

When it was time for Stella’s injection, my sweet girl became a little grouchy. The team handled her with such patience and compassion, moving us into a private room so they could safely care for her away from the open treatment area. That thoughtful accommodation meant so much to me.

We arrived at approximately 5:30 a.m. and were home within one to two hours. The cost was absolutely worth it to know my baby had been properly evaluated, treated, and relieved of her pain. I would definitely return, although I sincerely hope we never need another emergency visit!

Thank you, Dr. Russell, Nurse Shannon, and everyone at VEG Northern Liberties ER. You took wonderful care of my Stella, and I am eternally grateful.

EDIT: Had to add one more thing after some follow-up. I had some further questions and concerns about my dog a few days after our visit. I called at midnight hoping to speak with a vet. Dr. Russell answered the phone and without missing a beat asked, “How’s Scooby, what’s going on? How can I help?” I was blown away that I got a doc at midnight, she knew my dog, and was so willing to help. Dr. Russell answered my many questions and helped put my mind at ease. This team is absolutely SPECTACULAR. Words cannot describe the quality of care I’ve received from VEG.

Took our dog Scooby to VEG midday Saturday after some concerning symptoms. We were greeted and brought back right away, and met with a tech almost immediately after that. It was really busy and Scooby needed a lot of diagnostics so we were there for a while. While we waited we were checked on multiple times by multiple staff and offered comforts that made our time there more pleasant. Every single staff member there was hustling and working SO hard and despite it being so busy and (naturally) chaotic, we never felt rushed or felt stress from the team. Dr. Sturgill was a star. She was kind, truly loved and cared for our dog, and explained everything to me every step of the way. I truly felt like no question was silly and no request was too small. Dr. Sturgill and the VEG team were truly, truly wonderful. Thank you to Georgia for checking in on us and making us laugh. It's clear the team loves what they do, and they do it well! Won't be going anywhere else for emergency services and will be singing their praises to all my pet-owning friends. Thank you from Scooby and family!

The staff was very caring helpful and informative. Staff Was very understanding and took excellent care of my dog in most her weakest time. They even called the next day to check on how she was doing. Would recommend to everyone

Dr Russell and her team were exceptional. My visit on 8/15 was my second visit at this vet. I had an amazing experience with the staff and service here the first time that I knew to come back. The staff is always knowledgeable, understanding, kind, supportive and attentive during the visit. Dr Russell is an amazing vet and I’d trust her with any of my pets. Thank you guys for everything. 10/10 recommend.

Wonderful ER for pets and parents!  The staff couldn't have been nicer and the doctor was very informative and caring.   If your fur or feather baby needs emergency care, this is the place to go!  My little parakeet, Blue, had an accident and injured his eye.  Today he's flittering around the cage, giving Pete heck, eating and singing his little heart out!!  The doctor, the nurses, the staff and even the security guard were all great!  PS to Dr Chatterjee - I'll be sending Pete's bell video over shortly to make you smile!  Thanks to all of you!
I highly recommend this pet ER. VEG treated my cat Ace in a timely manner and the staff was amazing. Ace received meds and is now back to normal. Thank you again everyone!!

Great place to take your foolish kitty cat who eats a flower he's not supposed to. Was seen promptly upon arrival @ 9~am or so and was there until about 1pm. The doctor was in that time able to give us direction to call poison control to identify the flower, then on the fly create a treatment plan that involved X-Rays and bloodwork, both of which were carefully examined on-site.

For a Pet ER visit, and the level of work the foolish kitty cat had done, $1,500 felt fair in mister tumps america. The team provided excellent care and peace of mind. They offer financing options and are able to set up CareCredit and others on site for immediate payment processing,

They understand your stress and anxiety, and the team did their best to assuage that with snacks and drinks.

What could have been a much worse experience was made so much better by the amazing staff. They’re knowledgeable, thoughtful, and they truly care and understand that this is your baby they are taking care of. A clean, well-run place that, while I hope I never have to visit again, I would absolutely trust my cat with again.  Love that I could come and visit my baby whenever I wanted and could stay as long as I wanted. He would not be okay today without VEG. 6 out of 5 stars!
Everyone on staff at VEG is amazing.  From start to finish, I wouldn't change a thing about our experience there.

Words won't be able to encapsulates my gratitude for this amazing team, but I'll try. Bringing Theo, my little garbage disposal, in during such a scary and uncertain situation was overwhelming. But from the beginning, we were met with compassion, patience, kindness, and a breadth of knowledge that left my flabber gasted.

What meant the most to me was feeling like Theo was never just another patient. The team cared for him with such gentleness and attentiveness that it helped me feel confident that he was in the best possible hands. Dr. Chatterjee gave him a kiss on his forehead before surgery and it made me tear up (and jealous in a way I'll have to discuss in depth with my therapist later) that I had to blame allergies to preserve my reputation.

I hope with everything in me that I never have to see them again under the same circumstances, but I genuinely sleep better knowing they are there if we ever need them. I will always be grateful for the care they gave Theo and for the kindness they showed me during one of the most frightening experiences that, just to be clear, he did to himself. I mean come on, who eats FIVE squeakers, rocks, and an assortment of plastics??? Do you know how expensive his premium dog food and bone broth is 🤨

I brought my sick pup in last night and was taken very well care of. The staff are all so kind. My dog got all types of sick requiring lots of clean up. They were so kind and reassuring, not even batting an eye. I was there for about four hours on a Saturday night, part of the time there was just one doctor on. They did a great job getting my boy stabilized and offered me several clear options and were upfront on all fees (not cheap but when your animal is ill, does it matter!?). Great care, thank you all!

I have never made a google review but I felt like I needed to say how much I loved this place! Staff (Nurse Erin and Dr. Crowling) were extremely nice and helpful when I brought my cat in for an ear infection. They made my cat and I feel very comfortable and answered all of my questions. I even called back to ask the doctor a question and I was able to get ahold of her immediately. I was also expecting the cost to be very high but it was pretty reasonable! They also gave him a new toy! I wish they did routine vet appointments!!

Edit:

I came back again a couple years later and they are still just as amazing. I needed to come 3 nights in a row for bloodwork and they were so supportive and reassuring. Dr. Sturgill was amazing! They also do everything they can to maintain a positive environment and make you as comfortable as possible. They even called everyday to check in to see how my cat was doing. I still really wish they could be my primary vet!!

This Emergency Animal Hospital (VEG) in Willowgrove PA is awesome. They was there every step of the way with our beautiful 15 year old ShitzPoo "Handsome". First, in providing medical attention  two weeks prior; until lastly helping us make that final decision in sending him to doggie heaven. It was a weekend, lots of patients, and never once did we feel rushed nor in the way. The care, compassion and love shown to Handsome and my family did not go unnoticed. We thank the entire staff from the bottom of our hearts for their professionalism in maintaining our dignity "as we all" laid him to rest. Please note that the animal loving residents in Willowgrove PA are so grateful to have you. He will live on forever.  My baby boy Handsome, that brought 15 years & 4 months of sunshine

On July 29, 2026, I took my dog, Chase Alexander to the vet.  We had been here before and spent thousands on his care.  That day he had a lump in his throat which I thought was a foreign object. It blocked his airways.  They took him immediately, put him in an oxygen tank(?),  and came to me about over $3k worth of services for a tracheostomy amongst other things with no guarantee that he would live. I denied and they whispered.  I asked about euthanizing, taking him home, or other services. The Dr. told me that I should get an xray ($1k) so that she could see what was going on .  I told her that I could take him home after the xray and take it from there. Things changed after I said that I didn't want to pay for anything after the xray.  She tried to give him an IV and he fought against it so she said she would have to sedate him.  I asked her if it would make his breathing worse. She said that it "could stop his drive to breathe".  I told her if he started to pass, then they didn't need to revive him; just to let him rest in peace.  When they gave him the "sedation" (two shots),  he  IMMEDIATELY went into cardiac arrest, drooling, throwing up, and died a minute or two  later.  I was so confused on how quick it happened.  She was blank.  I WAS DEVASTATED They told me they could use the $1k toward his cremation and then give a refund.  When I got the receipt in the email ($117 refund), it didn't have any items, so I called.  I asked the woman that answered what services/meds they provided and she said they EUTHANIZED him!  I asked her to repeat it to see if I heard it correctly.  She said "well yes. we euthanized him. you signed off on it".  We DID NOT CONFIRM euthanizing.   I told her to send it and there was no euthanasia signing.  If they were going to euthanize him, why take the money for the x-ray? why not ask? why not let me say goodbye???? Cold hearted!!!!  I wouldn't even have known if I didn't call.

Expect to go in, be greeted, then sit there for hours while 2 staff people actually work and the rest eat, on laptops, shoot the breeze with each other.
Place is well staffed but most just sit and do nothing.
We walked out after 3 hours. I saw another bad review of the night staff. I had the same experience.

I haven’t needed to use emergency veterinary services until now, but I’m glad now that I have a good place to go if I have more problems for my dog.  The team at VEG ER were very quick and responsive.  We had no wait to bring our dog in, they were very attentive, and the cost was reasonable.  I’d recommend them.

I had to make a visit to veg when my cat started throwing up and refusing all food for over 24 hours. When I arrived, staff quickly whisked us in to a room where a tech took care of writing down the complaint and initial vitals. My cat and I were very comfortable waiting in our room.

Despite other patients requiring care at the moment, I felt like the visit was relatively quick and painless and the vet, Dr. Giana, came back with the diagnostic reports. Unfortunately I found out my cat was terminally ill and only had weeks left. Dr. Giana was gentle and empathetic when breaking the news. She was honest and transparent about his prognosis and did a phenomenal job explaining his test results. My experience with Dr. Giana made me feel well informed about his prognosis and confident in my decision to pursue palliative care with my cat’s happiness and comfort in mind.

Despite the devastating news no pet owner wants to hear, I felt that they allowed the experience to be as painless as possible for me and I truly appreciate it. My cat crossed the rainbow bridge almost 6 weeks later and I know he was as comfortable and happy as he could be given his circumstances.

If and when I have another pet, I’d choose veg for ER visits without hesitation in the future.

I want to sincerely thank The VEG ER for Pets. The staff were amazing and they showed so much compassion, and kindness towards me and my cat Jasper before he passed away. Losing a beloved pet is incredibly difficult, They allow you to stay with your pet, keeping them safe and comfortable…Amazing staff and the greatest support ever! Thank you, it meant so much to me and my family during that time, also the sympathy card you mailed was such a thoughtful and beautiful gesture that truly touched my heart. Thank you so much for treating my cat with such care and for showing so much compassion to me and our family.
I recommend for everyone to take your pets here…they will be truly loved and cared for by the staff. ❤️❤️❤️

My dog’s worsening condition went unaddressed for hours despite being visible, and at no point did anyone proactively check on him.

We were referred to this ER after another ER determined my dog needed evaluation by a soft tissue surgeon. He had recently undergone a dual anal sacculectomy, and I was concerned a surgical suture had come undone. At intake, I explained his surgery, medications, symptoms, and why we were referred there. Because this was already our second ER visit of the night, I explicitly confirmed numerous times whether they could provide the care he needed. I was directly reassured by the vet that she understood his situation and that the surgeon could help.

Unfortunately, we spent 3.5 hours waiting just to be told there had been a “miscommunication” and that they were not equipped to address his specific surgical complication after all. This was relayed by the same vet I spoke with at intake, and my dog's medical history and presenting problem had not changed during that 3.5-hour period.

During our 3.5 hours at VEG, my dog was actively bleeding, covered in feces, and repeatedly crying out in pain. A technician briefly checked his heart, lungs, and weight, then told me he was “stable.” However, no one inspected the surgical site, checked his temperature, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, or hydration status.

Because he was labeled “stable,” no one returned to reassess him despite ongoing bleeding and obvious distress. When I asked how “stable” had been determined without examining the source of the bleeding or checking for dehydration, I was told, “I can check his gums for you if you want, go ahead and lift them up.” We sat there covered in blood and feces. No one offered towels, wipes, pee pads, or basic assistance. I stayed with my dog because moving him worsened his pain and bleeding. Staff only came over when I signaled for assistance, and they repeatedly left without following through. Eventually, my family member had to call the hospital just to advocate for these basic supplies to be brought over.

In the midst of their own crises, other pet parents were startled by what was happening and repeatedly flagged down staff on my behalf. I never felt that any staff acknowledged the severity of my dog’s pain or the distress we were experiencing. The lack of compassion/empathy shown during such a frightening situation was deeply upsetting.

My dog had been bleeding and experiencing fecal incontinence for hours, soaking through countless pee pads while sitting in plain view. Had staff been regularly checking on him or taking my concerns seriously, the amount of blood loss would have been obvious. Later, staff acknowledged there was more bleeding than they initially realized.

My dog remained in severe pain throughout the wait. After the exam, the only help offered was sedation so he could tolerate the 1.5-hour drive back to his original surgeon, who could see him later that morning. Multiple staff members and I had to help restrain him so he could receive methadone injections for pain control. We spent the entire night at this ER waiting for care, only to leave and continue trying to get him help elsewhere.

I understand that there was only one vet on staff and that ER wait times can be lengthy. My concern is not the wait itself, but that during the visit my dog’s condition was not adequately assessed (despite hours of active bleeding, fecal incontinence, and initial assurance they could help). That delay prolonged his suffering and put him at unnecessary risk. I would not bring my dog back here or recommend this ER for urgent pet care.

Macey had a history of recurrent infections, including recurring UTIs, and at the time of hospitalization she was also dealing with an ear infection in addition to severe pneumonia. Over the course of more than 24 hours in the hospital, I watched her condition continue to decline while remaining on the same course of antibiotic treatment unbeknownst to us. What has stayed with me most is that when the overnight doctor came on shift, there appeared to be immediate concern and urgency around changing medications and escalating care due to suspicions of a antibiotic resistant virus. As someone who works in healthcare myself, that contrast has been difficult to reconcile emotionally and medically.

I understand that medicine is not always straightforward and that not every patient can be saved. I am not writing this to attack the clinic or claim certainty about what could have changed the outcome. But as both a pet owner and a healthcare professional, I do believe reassessment and timely escalation are critical when a hospitalized patient is actively deteriorating.

I loved my dog deeply, and watching her decline so rapidly while feeling uncertain about the treatment approach has left me with lasting questions and heartbreak.

My hope in sharing this is not to disparage the clinic, but to offer honest feedback from someone who entrusted them with a beloved family member during a medical crisis.

On 11/22 my boyfriend and I took our 10 year old yorkiepoo Joey here after he had been having diarrhea and vomiting for a few days and was starting to struggle to keep water down and we were worried.  However upon talking with the vet there that night she said “okay he’s been having diarrhea and vomiting for a few days… and?” Her tone felt very dismissive.  We stated that we believed he had pancreatitis because he had eaten a lot of fatty meat all in one sitting by accident the night before his symptoms started.  She said “maybe he does have pancreatitis” but didn’t seem to take it seriously.  She gave him some fluids in his back, a shot of anti-nausea meds, and sent us on our way.
Another thing worth noting about this place is that you are required to pay BEFORE receiving any treatment, which feels very strange and concerning, especially considering this place is an emergency room. ‼️

The next day Joey vomited again while on the anti-nausea med, which they told us to return for, so we went back again.

That was a huge mistake.

Upon bringing Joey back in, a different vet evaluated him, and said he had a grade 5/6 heart murmur, and somehow deduced that he was in heart failure after just one listen to his heart.
She did some blood work which revealed his kidney levels were pretty elevated — which we now know was from dehydration — but she was convinced he had kidney disease or kidney failure and stated that treating his kidneys would only hurt his heart and vice versa, and that it was too risky to treat him.  She then, after only working with us for about 20 minutes, suggested euthanizing Joey.  We said no, but she continued, saying “well, Joey is 10, so he’s definitely getting pretty old at this point, and you have to think about his quality of life”.  This felt like a painfully cold statement to make, especially since we had already told her that just prior to this Joey was in perfect health, and was still acting and looking like a puppy.
During this horrible conversation, a young couple left the room next to us carrying an empty carrier, and visibly crying.  The vet didn’t get up or anything, just looked over at them and said “bye guys, good luck!” with a very unempathetic tone.  Like, you can’t pause the conversation even for a second to go up to them and show them some empathy or humanity?  They obviously had just lost their fur baby.
After we said no to euthanasia, she then recommended we leave Joey with them overnight to try and help him, but said she couldn’t promise he’d make it through the night.  We said no because, why wouldn’t you recommend that BEFORE recommending we kill our dog?  Now how are we supposed to trust your intentions with him??
We then took Joey to Penn Vet Ryan hospital where they took amazing care of him, did an ultrasound and found no signs of heart disease or heart failure, he had an acute kidney injury from the dehydration but NOT kidney failure, and got the treatment he needed.  Joey is doing so much better now and will be making a full recovery.

Sunday, March 2nd, my daughter woke up to find our beloved dog, PO, unable to stand, lethargic, and struggling to breathe. His eyes were cloudy, and she was frantic. I quickly searched for the nearest emergency veterinary hospital, which led us to Veterinary Emergency Group.

She rushed him there with her sister, and they immediately took PO back for evaluation. After about an hour or two, they informed her that his lab tests and ultrasound results were normal. They administered IV fluids and then allowed her to see him. To her distress, PO was placed in a cone, visibly scared, and reacting out of fear.

The veterinarian then presented my daughter with a devastating decision: PO, only a year old, was now blind, would not improve, and was suffering. They strongly suggested euthanasia. My daughter was in tears and called me on FaceTime, unable to make such a decision without the children, who were all in school. The doctor told her she could bring the kids in to say their goodbyes but that keeping PO for six more hours would cost $2,200.

I told my daughter absolutely not—bring PO home. The hospital was against this decision and continued trying to convince her otherwise. When she stood firm, they required her to sign paperwork, stating that she was declining their recommendation. They also insisted on sedating PO due to his “aggression.” The final bill was $900.

When PO arrived home, he was shaking uncontrollably, unable to lift his head or see. The doctor had previously told my daughter they were unable to get his blood pressure, his pulse was low, and his temperature was dropping. Despite this grim prognosis, we refused to give up.

We immediately started a holistic approach, feeding him by syringe every two hours, taking turns caring for him throughout the night. Our entire family, including the grandkids, prayed together and showered PO with love and warmth.

From Sunday, March 2nd, to Thursday, March 6th, the transformation has been nothing short of miraculous. PO has gone from being unresponsive and weak to barking, standing, and regaining his energy. He is a completely different dog today—alive, thriving, and fighting.

This experience has taught us that while medical professionals have knowledge, they do not always have the final say. Trust your instincts. Don’t let fear or emotion cloud your judgment. Love, faith, and advocacy for our pets matter. We are forever grateful that we followed our hearts and brought PO home.
